hints: Notice the pH of 3 for X, what type of C4H8O2 compound is acidic enough to do that?
X must be unbranched butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, and Y must be propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$.
Join the acid part and the alcohol part together as an ester, $\text{RCO}_2\text{R'}$, keeping the straight chain on the left and the branched chain on the right.
walkthrough:
**Work out what X is**

Think like a detective. Formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ could be a carboxylic acid or an ester.

But an aqueous solution has pH about 3, so it is a weak acid. That tells us X is a carboxylic acid:
$$\text{RCOOH} \rightleftharpoons \text{RCOO}^- + \text{H}^+$$

**Use unbranched to pick the exact acid**

There are two C4 acids: straight chain butanoic acid and branched 2-methylpropanoic acid.

The question says unbranched carbon chain, so X must be:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Work out what Y is**

Y is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$ and a secondary alcohol.

The OH must be on the middle carbon, so Y is propan-2-ol:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$$

**Make the ester Z**

Carboxylic acid + alcohol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives an ester + water:
$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Put the butanoate part from X on the left and the isopropyl part from Y on the right. That gives $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

options.A: Incorrect. This has a branched acid part $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCO}_2$ and a straight-chain primary alcohol part $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It swaps both clues round, using branched acid instead of unbranched and primary alcohol instead of secondary.
options.B: Correct. Left side $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CO}_2$ is unbranched butanoate from X, right side $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ is the secondary isopropyl group from propan-2-ol. This is exactly the esterification product.
options.C: Incorrect. The acid part is correct for unbranched X, but the alcohol part $(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CH}_3$ is from propan-1-ol, a primary alcohol. Y was stated to be a secondary alcohol, so this cannot be Z.
options.D: Incorrect. The alcohol part is correct for secondary Y, but the acid part $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCO}_2$ is from branched 2-methylpropanoic acid. X was stated to have an unbranched chain, so this cannot be Z.
